findings.problem: The picture does not show what the captions say. The caption says 'The triangle stretches along the valley' and 'shrinks to a tiny triangle', but for almost the whole 13 s the Nelder-Mead triangle is a 10-30 px cluster of blue dots inside an orange finder ring on a 936 px plot; no purple triangle edges are readable. The one real stretch (rounds 7-13, a sliver of three dots in a line) lasts about 0.5 s (about 3.9-4.4 s) and the 'stretch' tag rides beside it for under a second; the second stretch (rounds 29-35) is already too small to see. The 'squeeze' tag is similar. A first-time learner sees a blue trail line and a ring, not a triangle changing shape, so the key idea of this scene (the triangle adapts its shape to the valley) is stated in words rather than drawn.
findings.fix: Add a fixed-size magnifier inset (for example a 300 px card in the empty lower-right of the plot, or top-left) that always draws the CURRENT triangle at a constant size, re-centred and rescaled each round, with its corner colours (green best, blue good, red worst) and the stretch / squeeze tag on it; connect it to the finder ring with a thin line. Give the first stretch 1.5-2 s instead of 0.5 s (adjust KEYS in the time warp) so the long thin triangle is seen, and keep the squeeze visible for 1.5 s. Alternatively zoom the plot view in on the triangle, as scene 7 does.
findings.evidence: algo-3-s9-1.9.png (two dots, no triangle), s9-3.4, s9-4.9, s9-6.4, s9-9.4 (ring around a few pixels); only s9@3.9-4.4 (algo-3-s9-4.0.png, 4.3.png) shows a stretched sliver of dots; s9@5.2/5.6 (stretch tag next to a ring around a point).

findings.problem: Unexplained symbols at the decisive moments. From the second corner the 'gain' card shows rows 's2' (-1) and later 's2' (-4/5) and 's1' (-3/5), and the ratio card shows a row called 'y-axis'. Slack variables are never introduced anywhere in the video (the storyboard says they are not shown), so s1 and s2 are meaningless to a first-time learner, yet the final stop test ('no direction gains: the corner is optimal', both rows red) depends on reading them. The card title 'gain per unit of z' is also opaque: gain of what, per what?
findings.fix: Replace the slack rows by plain-language directions that match arrows on the plot, for example 'along material edge +1' / 'back along x axis -1', or label them 'less material left' / 'less machine time left' with a one-line caption ('moving off a rule line gives up profit'). Retitle the card 'profit change if we move' (or 'profit per step') and rename 'y-axis' to 'y = 0 axis' or 'axis' with the marker drawn on the plot. Whatever the rows are called, draw each direction as a short arrow from the current corner (green when it gains, red when it loses) so the card and the plot say the same thing.

findings.problem: The method is never named where it is taught. The file and storyboard call it golden-section search, but scene 6's headline ('No slope needed: one new probe a step'), kicker ('BRACKETING'), chips and captions never say 'golden section'. The term first appears in scene 7: caption 'it homes in much faster than golden section', chip '4 golden', card 'golden width 0.146', and caption 'take a golden step instead'. The comparison that is scene 7's punchline therefore rests on a name the viewer was never given (bisection in scene 5 is never named either).
findings.fix: Name the method in scene 6: headline 'Golden section: one new probe a step' (or a sticker 'golden section' pinned top-left from the start), and use the same word in the first caption ('Golden section needs no slope, only heights'). In scene 5 add a 'bisection' tag or headline word the same way. Then scene 7's 'golden' chip and cards refer back to something the learner has seen.
findings.evidence: algo-3-s6-1.9.png, s6-3.4, s6-9.4, s6-12.4 (no mention); algo-3-s7-1.9.png (chips '4 golden'), s7-7.9 (caption 'golden section'), s7-12.4 ('golden width').

findings.problem: Pacing of the scene's centrepiece. The five test plans run at 1.1 s each (T0 5.6, STEP 1.1) and each plan's card is replaced before it can be read: row 1 appears at +0.2-0.5 s, row 2 at +0.5-0.8 s, the 'legal / not allowed' verdict at +0.8-1.0 s, and the whole card fades at +1.0-1.1 s, so the second sum and the verdict are fully visible for only about 0.2 s. Only the last plan (6, 1) stays on screen. 'Plug a plan into every rule' is the idea here, but a learner cannot read '8 <= 15', '11 <= 10' or the verdict, which breaks the brief's 'let each state sit about a second'. Plans (4, 3) and (5, 3) add little and flicker past.
findings.fix: Test three plans, not five, and give each about 2 s: (2, 2) legal, (1, 5) breaks rule 1, (6, 1) breaks rule 2 (keep (4, 3) and (5, 3) as dots only, or drop them). Hold both rows and the verdict for at least 1 s before the next plan; keep the finished plan's dot coloured on the plot. Show the substitution, not just the result: '4 + 2 x 3 = 10 <= 10' (or 2 + 2x2 = 6 <= 10) so 'plug in' is visible.
findings.evidence: algo-3-s2-6.5.png (first plan complete, 0.9 s in), s2-7.2.png (plan (4, 3): row 2 still empty), s2-8.png (plan (5, 3): both rows empty), s2-9.5.png (plan (1, 5): row 2 mid-pop); the verdicts for (4, 3), (5, 3) and (1, 5) never appear in any sampled still.

findings.problem: No story for the numbers. The scene says 'x + 2y <= 10' and '3x + y <= 15' with axes labelled only 'x' and 'y' and 'plan (2, 2)'. Nothing says that x and y are units of two products or that rule 1 is machine hours and rule 2 raw material. Scene 4 then suddenly talks about 'machine' and 'material' rows without saying which line is which (only a colour highlight links them afterwards). A first-time learner has no reason to care about the polygon.
findings.fix: Name the axes and rules once, in this scene: axis tags 'x = units of product X' and 'y = units of product Y' (or small icons), rule labels '1: machine hours x + 2y <= 10' and '2: raw material 3x + y <= 15' (shorten to fit at 28 px). Keep the names on the rule lines in scenes 3 and 4 so 'machine' and 'material' in the ratio card map to a line.
findings.evidence: algo-3-s2-5.png (labels '1: x + 2y <= 10', '2: 3x + y <= 15'), s2-6.5; algo-3-s4-3.4.png / s4-4.9.png ('machine', 'material' rows, unlabelled lines).

findings.problem: The key idea of the profit line, 'every point on the line earns the same score', is shown for under a second and never said. Three orange dots on the line z = 6 appear at 2.0-2.7 s and fade by 3.1 s, while the caption at that time says 'Each plan earns a score: z = 3x + 2y'. The pink dashed z = 21 line with the red cross ('misses the polygon') at 7.6-9.6 s is also unlabelled, so a learner cannot tell what the pink line or the cross mean.
findings.fix: Add a caption for the dots ('Every point on the line scores the same: 6') and keep the three dots, each tagged '6', for about 1.5 s. Label the pink line 'z = 21' and give the cross a tag 'no legal plan' (or 'leaves the region'); keep it up for 1.5 s.
findings.evidence: algo-3-s3-2.4.png (dots visible, caption about the formula), s3-3.4.png (dots gone); algo-3-s3-7.9.png and s3-8.3.png (unlabelled pink line and red cross).

findings.problem: The cards and the plot do not match. At (0, 0) the card lists 'x +3' and 'y +2' but only the x direction gets an arrow; at (5, 0) the card lists 'y +1' and 's2 -1' with a single arrow. The learner cannot see the second option being turned down. 'machine' / 'material' in 'how far can it grow?' have no counterpart on the plot until a line turns orange, and the ratio numbers (10, 5, 3, 15) are not marked where they happen on the axes. The right column also has a 170 px hole between the gain card and the profit card for the first 3.5 s and again at the end.
findings.fix: Draw both candidate directions from each corner (the chosen one orange and thick, the other grey and thin), and mark where each rule would stop the walk (small ticks at x = 5 and x = 10 on the x axis, at 'machine 3' and 'y axis' on the second edge). Pin the card slots so the profit card sits directly under whatever cards are showing (or move it under the plot), or reserve the gap for the ratio card from the first frame so the column does not jump.
findings.evidence: algo-3-s4-3.4.png (one arrow, two rows), s4-4.9.png (ratio card appears, no marks on the axis), s4-7.9.png, s4-1.9.png (gap between cards).

findings.problem: Abrupt change of problem with no bridge. After the LP (rules, polygon, corners) scene 5 opens on an unlabelled curve with no caption for the first 1.5 s; the viewer is never told that this is a new, one-variable problem (find the lowest point of f, no rules). There is also no x scale (the bracket width '1 ... 0.0625' refers to an axis with no numbers), the function is never named, and the method name 'bisection' is never used. The 'bracket width' counter tweens through values that are not real widths (0.3027 at s5@6.4 and 0.249 at s5@7.9), which looks like noise.
findings.fix: Start with a caption or tag that frames it: 'New problem: one number, no rules. Find the lowest point.' Label the start bracket 'a = 0' and 'b = 1' on the axis and say 'bisection' in the headline or a tag. Snap the width card to each real value with a pop instead of counting through intermediate decimals.
findings.evidence: algo-3-s5-0.4.png (empty frame, headline only), s5-1.9.png (first caption), s5-6.4.png ('bracket width 0.3027'), s5-7.9.png ('0.249').

findings.problem: The '× 0.618' chip appears at about 4.9 s but is not explained until the last caption at 11.2 s ('Every step keeps 0.618 of the bracket'). For six seconds the learner sees an orange chip next to a width that counts 0.809, 0.618, 0.382, 0.236, 0.146 without knowing what it means. The golden ratio itself (why the probes sit where they do) is never drawn.
findings.fix: Show the chip together with its caption the first time the width shrinks (about 4.5 s: 'Each step keeps 0.618 of the bracket'), and move the 'old probes are reused' caption after it. Optionally mark the probe positions as 0.382 and 0.618 of the bracket on the first step.
findings.evidence: algo-3-s6-4.9.png (chip next to 'width 0.809'), s6-7.9.png, s6-12.4.png (caption finally explains it).

findings.problem: The unsafe jump, the reason Brent needs a golden step, is on screen too briefly. The hollow ring for the rejected vertex and the red 'jump too big' sticker appear at 9.5-10.4 s (cross at 9.8, sticker faded by 10.4), about 0.6 s, and the golden probe arrives at 10.3 s. The reason ('step not shrinking') is not shown and the wording 'jump too big' differs from the lesson. The caption 'If a jump looks unsafe, take a golden step instead' stays up while nothing readable is happening.
findings.fix: Hold the ring, cross and sticker for 1.5-2 s, put the golden probe after it, and word the sticker as the lesson does ('step not shrinking'). Consider drawing the previous step's length as a bar next to the new jump so 'not smaller than before' is visible.
findings.evidence: algo-3-s7-9.8.png (ring only), s7-10.2.png (cross and sticker), s7-10.5.png (sticker already fading, golden probe 'x' popping), s7-10.9.png.

findings.problem: The payoff (same 7 evaluations, golden bracket 0.146 vs Brent 0.029, about 5 times tighter) is numbers only and has no caption: the last caption ends at 12.4 s while the cards pop in at 11.3-12.1 s, so for 1 s the caption still talks about unsafe jumps. The picture shows only one bracket (Brent's), so the comparison cannot be seen.
findings.fix: Replace the last caption with 'Same 7 tests, a bracket 5 times tighter' timed with the cards, and draw both brackets on the axis (golden's wide grey bar over Brent's narrow purple bar) so the difference is visible, not only printed.
findings.evidence: algo-3-s7-11.2.png (cards arriving under the 'unsafe' caption), s7-12.4.png and s7-12.8.png (no caption, two numbers).

findings.problem: The middle of the scene is cramped and the zoom is confusing. At 7.9 s the green b dot, the orange x probe, the vertex ring and the 'lower' tag all overlap at the curve minimum and the 'x' label is half hidden behind its own dot. The 'zoom ×2.4 / ×2.8 / ×15.8' chip is extra numeric noise and the view rescales three times, so the learner has to re-find a, b and c each time. After step 1 the new triple (a, b, c) has b and c almost touching (4.9 s).
findings.fix: Zoom in earlier (before step 2 lands) so the three points are always at least 60 px apart, and move the 'lower' tag to the side. Drop the numeric zoom chip, or replace it with a magnifier icon and the word 'zoomed in'.
findings.evidence: algo-3-s7-4.9.png (b and c overlap), s7-7.9.png (overlapping dots and labels), s7-6.4.png / s7-9.4.png (zoom chip).

findings.problem: Pacing: four moves and the shrink in 14 s. Round 2 (a repeat of the expand) takes 1.5 s in total (5.1-6.6 s), so R and E and their ticks flash by for about 0.3 s each; in round 3 the failed stretch ('E 5.82' with a cross) is visible for about 0.3 s before it is dropped at 8.2 s, although it is the point of the caption 'Stretched too far? Keep the plain flip'; in round 4 the overshooting flip ('R 11.89') shows for 0.3 s before the two contractions replace it. A first-time learner cannot read the verdicts that drive each rule.
findings.fix: Drop or shorten the repeat of round 2 (the caption can say 'Stretch again' over a quick replay) and spend that time on the failed stretch and the overshoot: hold the bad candidate with its cross for at least 1 s before it fades, and keep each caption on screen with its visual.
findings.evidence: algo-3-s8-6.4.png (R 3.89 and E 3.865 both ticking, fading), s8-8.3.png (E 5.82 with a cross, about to drop), s8-9.8.png (R 11.89, 0.3 s before it drops), s8-10.9.png.

findings.problem: Corner tags 'B', 'G', 'W' are never explained (best, good, worst) and they change places between rounds, so the same blue dot is 'G' in one frame and 'B' in the next. Colours help (green, blue, red) but the letters read as arbitrary. The grey diamond in the middle of the flip (the centroid) and the rings (curves of equal f) are also unlabelled; only 'lower f is better' is given.
findings.fix: On first appearance spell the roles out ('B best', 'G good', 'W worst') and add a tiny legend, or use full words on the tags in round 1. Label the diamond 'middle' and add 'rings: same f' to the 'lower f is better' tag.
findings.evidence: algo-3-s8-1.9.png (G 13.69, B 11.09), s8-3.4.png (W 17.09, grey diamond), s8-8.3.png (B and G now on other corners).

findings.problem: The shrink is shown without a cause. The previous round's contraction succeeded (M1 gets a tick at 10.9 s and the triangle is kept), then at 12.0 s the same triangle shrinks towards the best corner under the caption 'Nothing works? Shrink towards the best.' with a 'last resort' tag. Nothing in the picture failed, so a learner may think the algorithm shrinks after a good contraction.
findings.fix: Make the hypothetical explicit: re-show that triangle's flip and both contractions with red crosses ('all three fail') for a second, then shrink, or caption it 'If every try fails: shrink towards the best.' with the 'last resort' tag appearing before the motion.
findings.evidence: algo-3-s8-10.9.png (M1 ticked), s8-11.4.png (same triangle, contract chip lit), s8-12.4.png (shrink with 'last resort').

findings.problem: The method names are missing from the recap, and mostly from the whole video. The three cards read 'The best is a corner: simplex walks there', 'Trap the minimum, then shrink the trap' and 'No gradient needed: flip the worst corner'. Bisection, golden section, Brent and Nelder-Mead appear nowhere in the recap, so a learner has no names to attach to the pictures or to look up (and 'gradient' has not been used in the video before this).
findings.fix: Put the method name under each mini-figure as a tag: 'simplex', 'bisection and golden section (Brent adds parabolas)', 'Nelder-Mead'. Use 'slope' as in the video, or say 'no slope needed' to match scenes 5-9.
findings.evidence: algo-3-s10-4.9.png and s10-8.8.png (all three cards).

findings.problem: Five captions are too long for one line and wrap, leaving a one-word second line ('middle.', 'points.', 'section.', 'bowls.'): s6 'Add one probe a step. The lowest stays in the middle.', s7 'Same curve. Fit a parabola through the three points.' and 'Repeat: it homes in much faster than golden section.', s8 'Keep a triangle. Flip its worst corner through the middle.', s9 'Real problems have curved valleys, not simple bowls.'. Single-line captions elsewhere are at most about 50 characters. The orphan words look unfinished and the second line sits near the bottom edge.
findings.fix: Shorten each to 50 characters or fewer, for example 'One probe a step. The lowest stays in the middle.', 'Fit a parabola through the three points.', 'Repeat: much faster than golden section.', 'Flip the worst corner through the middle.', 'Real problems have curved valleys, not bowls.'.

findings.problem: Another unbridged jump: scene 8 starts on a contour map with a triangle and the caption 'Keep a triangle. Flip its worst corner through the middle.' with no statement that we now choose two numbers, that the rings are lines of equal value, or that there is no slope here. The star (the answer) is drawn from the first frame, while the series convention is that the optimum appears only when found.
findings.fix: Add an opening line such as 'Two numbers to choose, no slopes: use a triangle.' and fade the star in only after the last move (or keep it deliberately and tag it 'target' for the explanation).
findings.evidence: algo-3-s8-0.4.png (rings and a triangle only), s8-1.9.png (star already present).

findings.problem: Corner pills overlap their own dots ((0, 5), (0, 0), (5, 0) touch the blue dots by 10-15 px), the moving profit line passes under the '(0, 5)' pill at z = 13, and a stray orange dash pokes out under the '(5, 0)' pill beyond the axis at z = 18.
findings.fix: Offset the pills by another 10-14 px, and clip the profit line to the plot area (or end it at the axis) so no dash appears below the axis labels.
findings.evidence: algo-3-s3-1.9.png, s3-4.9.png (line crosses the (0, 5) pill), s3-6.4.png (dash near (570, 803)).

findings.problem: The optimum star lands about 45 px above the green corner (4, 3) instead of on it and stays floating there, unlike scene 3 where it sits exactly on the corner; the polygon also changes scale and tick range between scenes 3 and 4 (axes to 7 versus to 6), which reads as a jump cut.
findings.fix: Place the star on the corner and keep the scene 3 plot size and view (give the cards less width instead).
findings.evidence: algo-3-s4-12.4.png and s4-13.9.png (star above the dot) versus algo-3-s3-7.9.png (star on the corner).

findings.problem: The contour map has tracing artefacts: a stray tick near (265, 330) and hairpin fragments near (395, 600) and (500, 705) where marching-squares lines end inside the valley, which look like dirt. The top stat cards sit on top of the contours at the centre of the map.
findings.fix: Clean or drop the unclosed contour fragments (raise grid resolution or discard segments shorter than a threshold) and move the two stat cards to the empty top-left or right area.
findings.evidence: algo-3-s9-1.9.png and s9-12.8.png.

findings.problem: The sub line 'How to find the best answer' says what the phase is about, not what it changed; the brief asks the sub line to carry the real-world payoff (compare 'How Google ranks the web'). Nothing in the video shows where optimisation is used.
findings.fix: Use a payoff line such as 'How factories, routes and AI find the best plan', or add one short payoff line to the recap.
findings.evidence: algo-3-s1-3.8.png.

findings.problem: Right column balance: the checker card and verdict sit in the upper 300 px next to a 600 px plot and the lower right of the stage (y 650-870) is empty for the whole scene (same in scene 3 for the first 7 s).
findings.fix: Keep a running list of the plans tested (small dot chips 'legal / not allowed') in the empty area, or centre the checker vertically against the plot.
